carousels.title: Housing Starts Jump, Permits Dip: What It Means for Supply
carousels.cover_text: Starts Up, Permits Down: Red Flag?
carousels.caption:
Everyone's celebrating the 19% jump in June housing starts, but the permit data tells a different, more concerning story. As an underwriter, I see this as a red flag for future housing supply and builder sentiment. It's a disconnect that could mean less inventory down the road, impacting both purchase pipelines and home values. Don't get caught flat-footed – understand what this data really means for your market and your clients.

Source : https://tinyurl.com/24ovfcg5
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #housingmarket #newconstruction #realestateinvesting
carousels.hook: June's Housing Starts: A Misleading Win?
carousels.what_happened: June housing starts jumped 19% to 1.3 million, largely due to multifamily construction. However, building permits simultaneously fell 3% to 1.367 million.

breakdown.heading: The 'Starts' Surge
breakdown.body: The 19% rise in starts is mostly multifamily projects, which tend to be large and move quickly once approved. This boosts the headline number significantly.

breakdown.heading: Permits: The Real Indicator
breakdown.body: Permits are a forward-looking metric. A 3% drop signals that fewer projects are entering the pipeline, which means less future supply in 6-12 months.

breakdown.heading: Underwriting's View
breakdown.body: As an underwriter, I'd look past the starts number. The permit decline tells me builders are still cautious, and the pipeline for *new* projects is shrinking.

breakdown.heading: Builder Sentiment Aligns
breakdown.body: Builder confidence also fell, staying near post-recession lows. This sentiment aligns with the permit data, not the surge in starts, indicating ongoing uncertainty.

carousels.my_take: The June housing starts headline is like celebrating a sprint win while ignoring the marathon. Permits are down, and builder confidence is low – that’s the real story for future inventory.
carousels.action_lo: Educate referral partners that new construction supply might tighten again soon; help them set realistic buyer expectations.
carousels.action_realtor: Focus on finding existing inventory and connect with builders on their *committed* pipeline, not just current starts.
carousels.cta_question: Are you seeing a real pickup in new construction *projects*, or just completions of older ones?

carousels.title: Non-QM Loans Get Sophisticated: What It Means for Borrowers
carousels.caption:
Non-QM loans are often seen as high-risk, but a new advanced credit risk model from RiskSpan could change that perception. This isn't just a tech upgrade; it's a signal of growing sophistication and stability in the non-QM market. For those serving self-employed borrowers or investors, this could translate to more consistent approvals and potentially better pricing, as lenders gain a clearer picture of true risk. Stay informed on how these models refine the underwriting process.

Source : https://tinyurl.com/2d2ahsmf
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #nonqm #mortgagebroker #realestateinvesting
carousels.hook: Non-QM's New Model: Is the Market Maturing?
carousels.what_happened: RiskSpan launched Credit Model 7.1 specifically for non-QM (non-qualified mortgage) loans. This model was trained on $87 billion in unpaid principal balance (UPB) of non-QM loans.

breakdown.heading: What is Non-QM?
breakdown.body: Non-QM loans are for borrowers who don't fit standard agency guidelines (e.g., self-employed, investors). They offer flexibility but have historically been harder to price for risk.

breakdown.heading: The Data Advantage
breakdown.body: Training on $87B UPB means this model has a massive dataset. It allows for much more accurate risk assessment than traditional FICO scores or manual reviews alone.

breakdown.heading: Underwriting Impact
breakdown.body: As an underwriter, this means faster, more consistent decisions on complex files. It reduces the 'gray area' and brings more objectivity to non-QM approvals.

breakdown.heading: Market Legitimacy
breakdown.body: Sophisticated models like this signal a maturing non-QM market. Better risk management attracts more institutional capital, potentially stabilizing product availability and pricing.

carousels.my_take: This new non-QM credit model isn't just about better tech; it's about legitimizing a vital market segment. It should lead to more predictable underwriting and broader access for deserving borrowers.
carousels.action_lo: Deepen your understanding of non-QM guidelines and lenders using advanced models to confidently serve niche borrowers.
carousels.action_realtor: Partner with LPs (loan officers) fluent in non-QM to capture more self-employed clients and real estate investors.
carousels.cta_question: How will enhanced risk modeling change your approach to non-QM borrowers?

carousels.title: The Next Refi Window: Faster Than You Think
carousels.cover_text: Refi Window: Blink and Miss It.
carousels.caption:
Everyone is waiting for the next refinance boom, but NMP is right: it could open and close faster than most pipelines are ready for. The last mini-window in February showed how quickly rates can shift due to external events. As an underwriter, I see lenders needing to be nimble, with strong tech and clear processes, to capitalize. Don't let your team get caught flat-footed; agility will be the name of the game when rates drop. Are you prepared?

Source : https://tinyurl.com/26rhwgho
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #mortgagerates #refinance #loanofficer
carousels.hook: The Next Refi Window: Are You Actually Ready?
carousels.what_happened: National Mortgage Professional warns that the next refinance window will open fast and could close even faster. Many pipelines are not prepared to handle this rapid shift.

breakdown.heading: Past as Prologue
breakdown.body: In February, 30-year fixed rates hit 6.01%, their lowest since September 2022. Refi apps more than doubled year-over-year, but the window closed quickly due to geopolitical events.

breakdown.heading: Rate Volatility is Key
breakdown.body: Today's market reacts sharply to news. Rates can drop on inflation reports or rise on global events, creating brief, unpredictable opportunities.

breakdown.heading: Underwriting's Challenge
breakdown.body: For underwriters, a fast refi wave means pressure on turn times. Pipelines need to be streamlined and staffed for surge capacity, or loans will bottleneck.

breakdown.heading: The 'Ready' Pipeline
breakdown.body: Lenders need robust tech, efficient processes, and well-trained staff to capture these quick windows. Waiting to staff up is too late.

carousels.my_take: The next refi opportunity won't be a prolonged flood, but a series of quick, powerful tides. If your processing isn't dialed in, you'll be leaving money on the table.
carousels.action_lo: Build a 'warm call' list of past clients. Have your CRM ready to identify and contact potential refinances instantly when rates dip.
carousels.action_realtor: Understand that lower rates can boost buyer purchasing power, even if short-lived. Stay connected with LPs who can move fast.
carousels.cta_question: What specific operational changes are you making to ensure your team is ready for a rapid refi surge?
